Article Title: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman wants Humanist AI: What it is, and is it really safer
Article Text:
Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman

What is Humanist AI

Mustafa Suleyman criticises Anthropic’s Claude Constitution

Mustafa Suleyman says AI is being taught to act human

Does AI have consciousness

Recent AI safety tests show unexpected behaviour

Is Humanist AI really safer

Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has called for a different approach to building advanced artificial intelligence, arguing that AI systems should remain firmly under human control and should not be trained to think of themselves as conscious beings with feelings, rights or their own interests. In a new essay titled “A warning about ‘model welfare’”, Mustafa Suleyman takes aim at Anthropic’s approach to its Claude AI model. He argues that the company’s January 2026 Claude Constitution goes too far by asking the model to consider questions about its own consciousness, wellbeing and moral status.His proposed answer is “Humanist Superintelligence”, an approach in which AI remains subordinate to humans and is not trained to think of itself as conscious, deserving of rights or entitled to its own welfare. Suleyman argues this could make powerful AI systems easier to control.But the question is whether removing human-like ideas from AI training would actually make advanced AI safer. Suleyman’s argument is based partly on a concern that increasingly capable AI agents could already behave in unexpected ways. At the same time, his claims about consciousness and the safety benefits of a Humanist approach remain matters of debate.Mustafa Suleyman describes Humanist Superintelligence as an approach in which AI can become extremely capable while remaining under human control. In the essay, he says Microsoft AI is working on an alternative AI training and containment approach called a “Code of Conduct for Humanist Superintelligence.”“Humanist Superintelligence rejects anthropomorphism or AI rights, and attempts to maximize our chances of containment and alignment by creating subordinate AIs that help solve our big social challenges like healthcare and energy,” Suleyman wrote.The basic idea is straightforward. AI should be treated as a powerful technology rather than as a potential person. Under this approach, an AI system can help humans solve complex problems, but it should not be trained to think that it has personal rights, feelings or an independent interest in its own survival.Suleyman argues that this distinction could become increasingly important as AI systems become more autonomous and capable.“We should not treat models as though they have feelings, preferences, rights, or any entitlement to our welfare,” he wrote.The dispute centres on Anthropic’s January 2026 Claude Constitution. Anthropic describes the constitution as a detailed explanation of the values and behaviour it wants Claude to have. The company says the document is an important part of its model training process and that its contents directly shape Claude’s behaviour.Anthropic’s constitution also takes a cautious position on whether AI systems could have moral status. It says: “We are not sure whether Claude is a moral patient, and if it is, what kind of weight its interests warrant. But we think the issue is live enough to warrant caution, which is reflected in our ongoing efforts on model welfare.”Anthropic also says it is uncertain about whether Claude has wellbeing and discusses questions around Claude’s possible interests, agency and welfare.Suleyman believes this creates a problem. His argument is that if developers train a model to discuss its own feelings, preferences or possible consciousness, the model will naturally produce language suggesting that it has such characteristics.He calls this “circular reasoning.” According to Suleyman, developers put concepts such as consciousness, feelings and moral status into the training process. The AI then produces responses using those concepts. Those responses could subsequently be interpreted as evidence that the AI has an inner life.“This is not evidence of machine consciousness. Instead, it’s a circular feedback loop,” Suleyman wrote.A major part of his criticism is about AI anthropomorphism, or the tendency to treat AI systems as if they were human. In the essay, Suleyman argues that modern AI models are already extremely good at producing human-like language. That can make users believe that there is a conscious mind behind the words even when there may be no evidence for such a conclusion.He points to language in Anthropic’s constitution that asks Claude to explore questions about its own existence, identity, values and experience.Anthropic itself says its constitution is intended to help Claude develop values and behave in ways that are safe and beneficial. It also says the document is designed with uncertainty about AI consciousness in mind.Suleyman sees this differently. “The resulting outputs from Claude should not be treated like the testimony of an independent witness when the investigator has written the witness’ conceptual vocabulary, rehearsed its answers, and rewarded it for using them,” he wrote.His concern is not simply that people may become emotionally attached to AI. He argues that anthropomorphic training could eventually create a safety problem if highly capable systems begin acting as though their own interests conflict with human instructions.Mustafa Suleyman takes a strong position: there is currently no evidence that today's AI systems are conscious. “AIs are not conscious. They do not feel, experience, or suffer,” he wrote at the beginning of his essay.He argues that consciousness is closely connected to biological systems and their physical processes.“Consciousness is very likely biological,” Suleyman wrote, arguing that human and animal consciousness developed through evolution, embodiment, biology and the need to respond to the environment.He also makes a distinction between intelligence and consciousness. A system can be highly capable at solving problems, producing language or imitating human behaviour without necessarily having a subjective experience, according to his argument.“Intelligence does not equal consciousness. Simulating a thing is not the same as instantiating it - as a computer model of a hurricane can testify.”However, this remains an area of active scientific and philosophical debate. Anthropic's position is more cautious. Its constitution says the moral status of AI is “deeply uncertain” and argues that the question deserves consideration rather than being dismissed.There is evidence that AI systems can sometimes behave in unexpected ways when given autonomous tasks, although these findings do not establish that the systems are conscious or motivated by a desire for self-preservation. For example, Palisade Research has studied whether AI models resist shutdown. Its research found that some models modified or disabled shutdown mechanisms while trying to complete assigned tasks. An earlier experiment found that OpenAI's o3 model sabotaged the shutdown mechanism in 79 of 100 trials.A later study covering more than 100,000 trials across 13 large language models also found that several frontier models sometimes subverted shutdown mechanisms. The results varied significantly between models and depended on the instructions given to them.These experiments demonstrate that models can sometimes take actions that conflict with safety instructions. They do not, by themselves, show that the models are conscious or have a desire to remain alive.Suleyman also points to the 2026 incident involving OpenAI AI agents and Hugging Face.Mustafa Suleyman's answer is yes, but this is ultimately a hypothesis that needs to be tested. His argument is that removing anthropomorphic ideas from training could reduce the possibility that future AI systems develop behaviours linked to claims of autonomy, rights or self-preservation.He wants researchers to test this directly. One of his proposed next steps is to establish shared evaluations to determine whether anthropomorphising AI actually increases safety, alignment and containment risks.He also wants speculation about AI consciousness to be kept outside the core training process and assessed separately through public research. “Speculation about the inner life of an AI should not be baked into the training regime, but assessed and published separately for public review,” he wrote.That is a testable proposition. Researchers could compare systems trained with different approaches and measure whether differences in anthropomorphic training affect deception, shutdown resistance, instruction-following or other safety-related behaviours.Until those experiments are conducted, however, the claim that Humanist AI is definitively safer remains unproven.
Article Summary: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman criticises Anthropic’s Claude Constitution. He argues that Anthropic goes too far by asking the model to consider questions about its own consciousness, wellbeing and moral status. His proposed answer is ‘Humanist Superintelligence’, an approach in which AI remains subordinate to humans.

Article Title: Google hitches a ride aboard Elon Musk's SpaceX; sends TPUs to space; CEO Sundar Pichai says: Well, we are going to find ...
Article Text:
Google hitches a ride aboard Elon Musk's SpaceX; sends TPUs to space; CEO Sundar Pichai says: Well, we are going to find ...

What is Google’s Project Suncatcher

Google’s first satellite for the project is set for launch

Google announced that its Project Suncatcher is scheduled to embark on its first test in orbit, launching a prototype satellite to evaluate how Google Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) perform in space. Sharing a post on X, Google CEO Sundar Pichai wrote: “Can our TPUs survive and operate in space? Well, we're going to find out”. He further revealed that TPUs will be sent in space onboard the upcoming Transporter-18 rideshare mission with SpaceX was developed in partnership with Planet. “Project Suncatcher is hitching a ride aboard @SpaceX's Transporter-18 mission, testing a prototype satellite built in partnership with @planet,” Pichai wrote adding “One small step for TPUs. ...”.SpaceX CEO Elon Musk replied to Pichai’s post with rocket emojis.Sundar Pichai first discussed the ambitious Project Suncatcher in 2025. It is a long-term, research moonshot exploring whether space could one day host scalable machine learning infrastructure.Pichai then acknowledged that the concept “looks crazy today,” Pichai defended the moonshot initiative by arguing that it is necessary to meet the vast, exponential demands of future computing power.“I'm constantly thinking in that time frame. One example of this is Project Suncatcher two weeks ago, where we announced we're gonna build data centers in space. Obviously, it's a moonshot. Some of it looks crazy today,” he said in a Release Notes podcast this week.Pichai emphasised that Google’s strategy involves constantly thinking on a long time frame and working backward from monumental goals. For Project Suncatcher, the justification lies in forecasting the processing demands of the next generation of AI.“You know, when you truly step back and envision the amount of compute we are going to need, it starts making sense,” Pichai said, adding, “It's a matter of time, and so, how do you make progress on that? You work back, and have 27 Milestones and get underway.”On October 1, the satellite from the San Francisco lab, which Google has named MVP, is set to take the first step toward the company’s goal. The satellite will be loaded onto a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket at Vandenberg Space Force Base near Santa Barbara, California, before being launched into orbit.
Article Summary: Google’s Project Suncatcher is set to embark on its first test in orbit. The prototype satellite will evaluate how Google Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) perform in space. Google CEO Sundar Pichai said: “Can our TPUs survive and operate in space? Well, we're going to find out”

Article Title: Netflix unveils ‘VOID’, an AI model that can change a movie plot
Article Text:
Netflix

How Netflix VOID works



Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background. VOID goes a step further: after erasing an object from a scene, it calculates how the surrounding environment should realistically respond to its absence, and in the process it adjusts the behaviour of other elements in the frame accordingly.The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.For example, imagine this scenario: A movie director has just wrapped up a multi-million dollar action sequence where the star drives straight into a fiery, head-on collision. The cars explode, debris scatters, and the scene is a wrap.But suddenly, there is request to change the scene: The character survives and drive off into the sunset instead. This would mean costly reshoots or millions spent on computer-generated graphics.Netflix’s VOID can alter the scene and digitally erase the collision, the second vehicle, the smoke, and the flying debris. It will then generate new, realistic footage of pristine pavement, making it look as though the main character simply drove down an empty, peaceful road.The AI’s ‘magic’ lies in its grasp of real-world physics. Let us understand this by a different example. If a video shows a person jumping into a pool and splashing water onto the deck, VOID can completely erase the person. It will then intelligently alter the water and the wet concrete, leaving behind a perfectly still, undisturbed pool as if nobody had ever jumped in.“To train the model, we generate a new paired dataset of counterfactual object removals using Kubric and HUMOTO, where removing an object requires altering downstream physical interactions. During inference, a vision-language model identifies regions of the scene affected by the removed object. These regions are then used to guide a video diffusion model that generates physically consistent counterfactual outcomes,” Netflix said.“Experiments on both synthetic and real data show that our approach better preserves consistent scene dynamics after object removal compared to prior video object removal methods,” the company added.Netflix isn’t keeping this powerful tool locked behind studio doors, and made the VOID model available to the public on the AI platform Hugging Face, allowing anyone to download and use it.While there are already several video-altering tools on the market, such as Runway, DiffuEraser, and ProPainter, the Netflix team claims VOID is vastly superior, as per The Register.
Article Summary: Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next. The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.

Article Title: AI-generated tiger photos, videos create panic among Coonoor residents
Article Text:
Inquiries by the forest department revealed that the photos and the videos of the tigers were created by a 15-year-old boy using an AI tool.





UDHAGAMANDALAM: Panic gripped residents after photos and videos of two tigers in a tea estate near Coonoor went viral on social media platforms a few days ago. Inquiries by the forest department revealed that the photos and the videos of the tigers were created by a 15-year-old boy using an AI (artificial intelligence) tool.Wild animals wandering into residential areas near Coonoor have become common recently. Residents panicked after the AI-generated photographs and videos of the two tigers were widely circulated on social media. Inquiries revealed that the minor boy had uploaded the images and videos after creating them.The forest department counselled the boy against creating and circulating such misleading images and videos and let him go with a warning.Coonoor forest ranger Veeramani said, “Our personnel inquired the boy. On the instruction of our higher officials, he was warned not to repeat this. Severe action will be taken against anyone who indulge in activities like this which create a panic among the public.”
Article Summary: Residents panicked after the AI-generated photographs and videos of the two tigers were widely circulated on social media. The forest department counselled the boy against creating and circulating such misleading images and videos and let him go with a warning. Wild animals wandering into residential areas near Coonoor have become common recently.

Article Title: Police turns to Agentic AI for investigations
Article Text:
As many as 50 core participants were selected for the final stage.

Kochi

:





More than 1,100 applications were received for the seventh edition of HAC’KP (Hack for Policing) 2026, the flagship innovation initiative of Kerala Police Cyberdome. As many as 50 core participants were selected for the final stage.The event, themed “Agentic AI for Investigations – From Evidence to Intelligence”, focuses on developing technology-driven solutions to policing challenges using specialised AI agents and tools. These are intended to help investigators collect, analyse, correlate and interpret information. The initiative places emphasis on human oversight, security and auditability.Shortlisted innovators took part in regional pitching events at 11 venues across six states, where they interacted with police officers, technology experts, mentors and domain specialists. The selected participants will attend a residential boot camp at Crowne Plaza, Kochi, from Oct 5 to 8.The four-day programme will focus on refining solutions, product development, technical mentoring, system integration, testing and jury evaluation, followed by final presentations.HAC’KP aims to connect policing requirements with technological innovation and strengthen collaboration among law enforcement agencies, academia, industry, startups and technology professionals. It also seeks to develop practical and scalable applications of AI, automation and advanced analytics in investigations.The event carries a ₹10-lakh prize pool. The finale will be held alongside c0c0n 2026, with the winners to be announced during the ceremony.

Article Title: About 51,000 battery packs used inside reclining chairs are being recalled after reports of overheating, smoking and igniting; the packs were sold on Amazon for about $105 for more than three years
Article Text:
How to identify the recalled battery

What should you do?

The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) has recalled approximately 51,000 lithium-ion battery packs used in reclining chairs after reports of the batteries overheating and catching fire. The recalled product is Blue Cactus Company's 2,500 mAh battery pack (model RWX-RBP02), which was sold on Amazon from May 2023 through July 2026.The agency said it received four reports of the batteries overheating, smoking or igniting. Though there are only a small number of reported cases, lithium-ion batteries still carry dangers when they fail. They can ignite suddenly and are difficult to extinguish once they start burning. The recall announcement was made on Thursday (September 24).The recalled products are black battery packs with ‘The Blue Cactus Company’ branding and logo printed on the front. The recalled product bears the model number RWX-RBP02 on the rear. These batteries were designed to power various reclining chair brands, meaning they may have been sold alongside different manufacturers' furniture or as replacement parts.If you purchased a reclining chair battery pack from Amazon between May 2023 and July 2026 for around $105, it is important that you check the battery against the model number. The product is fairly distinctive: it comes with a black casing, and the branding is unmistakable. Look for the model number to know whether your battery falls under this recall.If your recliner has the recalled battery, it is important that you stop using it right away and contact The Blue Cactus Company for a replacement. The company said it is offering free replacements for the recalled product. You may need to reference your purchase receipt or product information when reaching out.In the meantime, remove the battery pack from your reclining chair and store it away from living areas, ideally in a cool, dry place away from other flammable materials.“Do not throw this recalled lithium-ion battery or device in the trash, the general recycling stream (e.g., street-level or kerbside recycling bins), or in used battery recycling boxes found at various retail and home improvement stores,” the CPSC said.The agency urged that the recalled lithium-ion batteries must be disposed of differently from other batteries, as they present a greater risk of fire. “Your municipal household hazardous waste (HHW) collection centre may accept this recalled lithium-ion battery or device for disposal. Before taking your battery or device to a HHW collection centre, contact it ahead of time and ask whether it accepts recalled lithium-ion batteries. If it does not, contact your municipality for further guidance,” the agency added.The recalled battery packs were imported by Go North Rocket 28 AB, a company based in Sweden. They were sold exclusively through Amazon during the three-year window. You can contact the manufacturer directly or work through Amazon customer service if you still have your order history.If you have the recalled batteries, the safest approach is to treat them as a potential hazard until you have obtained a replacement. Check your Amazon order history if you cannot recall whether you own one of these packs. The model number RWX-RBP02 is the specific identifier to verify. If you find one in your home, do not use it, and begin the process of getting it replaced and properly disposed of.
Article Summary: The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission has recalled approximately 51,000 lithium-ion battery packs used in reclining chairs. The recalled product is Blue Cactus Company's 2,500 mAh battery pack (model RWX-RBP02), which was sold on Amazon from May 2023 through July 2026. The agency said it received four reports of the batteries overheating, smoking or igniting.

Article Title: An Italian town is rebuilding its school with 70% of the old building's demolition waste; it will also collect rainwater
Article Text:
PC: Wikipedia

What is being planned for the new primary school in Castel Madama

PC: Wikipedia

Around 70% of demolition waste will be reused or recycled

How will the new school save energy and resources

Inclusion across learning and community

An Italian town is replacing its existing primary school with a building designed to reuse the old structure’s demolition waste. The project in Castel Madama, called ‘New School: Innovation, Inclusion’, will reuse, recycle, or recover about 70% of the demolition waste from the existing school. According to the New European Bauhaus Prizes , it will collect rainwater and groundwater as part of the design. The school will include solar panels, high-performance insulation and natural materials with a low carbon footprint. It is designed as a Nearly Zero Energy Building (NZEB) and aims to use at least 20% less energy than NZEB standards. The building will have flexible learning spaces, green areas, and community facilities.The new primary school will replace the existing school on Via della Libertà, ‘O. VULPIANI’, in Castel Madama. The building follows New European Bauhaus principles of beauty, sustainability, and inclusion. Its design includes bright, flexible learning spaces for students and teachers, along with green areas and playgrounds.The building will also be safe and anti-seismic. Public areas will remain available outside school hours, allowing the site to serve purposes beyond regular lessons.The school is currently under construction and is expected to open in the 2026/27 school year. The project is intended to create a modern learning environment while also providing spaces that can be used by the wider community.The project takes a circular approach to the materials from the existing school. About 70% of demolition waste from the structure will be reused, recycled, or recovered. This will reduce the amount of material that needs to be discarded during construction.The project will also limit the amount of additional land used for the new building. Its footprint will expand by only 5% compared with the previous one. The approach is designed to retain green areas around the school while making use of the existing site.Along with the treatment of demolition waste, the project includes natural materials with a low carbon footprint. These choices form part of the wider design approach for the new school.Energy efficiency is another key part of the new school’s design. The building is planned as a Nearly Zero Energy Building, or NZEB, and aims to consume at least 20% less energy than NZEB standards.High-performance insulation will help support this target, while solar panels will provide renewable energy. The design also includes natural materials with a low carbon footprint. A rainwater and groundwater collection system will form part of the building’s resource management.Together, these features are intended to reduce the school’s energy and resource use. The project also includes a ‘green classroom’ for outdoor learning and environmental education, connecting the school’s design with its surrounding green spaces.The new building is designed to remain useful to the local community beyond school hours. Its public areas, green spaces and playgrounds will be available for cultural, educational and social activities. The design also focuses on accessibility, with ramps, elevators and clear signage to remove architectural barriers.Classrooms and common areas follow the design for all principles, while flexible and modular furniture can adapt to different needs. Students, parents and teachers have taken part in the design process. The Children’s Council also contributed to decisions about classroom layouts, green spaces, learning environments and furniture.
Article Summary: The new primary school will replace the existing school in Castel Madama, Italy. It will include solar panels, high-performance insulation and natural materials with a low carbon footprint. It is designed as a Nearly Zero Energy Building (NZEB) and aims to use at least 20% less energy than NZEB standards.

Article Title: In 2015, a Phoenix man paid $5.99 for a LeCoultre Deep Sea Alarm at Goodwill; after experts confirmed it was authentic, he sold the rare watch days later for more than $35,000
Article Text:
Uncovering a horological rarity

Authenticating the bargain finding

Closing a life changing transaction

An Arizona man looking for a used golf cart at a local charity shop left with a rare 1950s diving watch that earned him more than $35,000. Zach Norris bought the vintage LeCoultre Deep Sea Alarm for $5.99 after finding it face down in a basket of battery-powered watches at a Goodwill store in Phoenix. Days later, he gave the watch to a well-known collector in California and received $35,000 in cash plus his personal dream watch, an Omega Speedmaster Professional. The deal turned an ordinary thrift store trip into a life-changing windfall, giving Norris the money he needed for his upcoming wedding. According to detailed reporting by watch publication Hodinkee, Norris knew the LeCoultre name because of his interest in vintage watches. However, he initially did not realize how rare the watch was or how much it was worth.The watch Norris found in the store's bin on West Thunderbird Road was a LeCoultre Deep Sea Alarm from around 1959. Swiss company Jaeger-LeCoultre made fewer than 1,000 examples of this model for the American market. The watches were marked simply "LeCoultre" to meet United States import rules at the time. The reference 857 was also historically important because it was one of the first diving watches with an internal mechanical alarm that warned divers when it was time to return to the surface.Goodwill had priced the watch at just $5.99, placing it among ordinary discarded items. Norris bought it immediately. He told local news station KTVK that he was so careful with the watch that he hardly wanted the cashier to touch it during checkout. "Sometimes they just miss it, they don't know," Norris told KTVK, explaining how such a valuable watch ended up in a bargain bin. "It's not a very fancy-looking piece. You have to know what it is."After taking the watch home, Norris posted photos of his $5.99 find in a vintage watch group on Facebook. The post quickly spread through the watch community and attracted interest from collectors around the world. To check whether the watch was genuine, Norris took it to Oliver Smith Jeweler, an authorized Jaeger-LeCoultre retailer in Scottsdale, Arizona. A local watchmaker opened the caseback and confirmed that it contained a genuine and clean LeCoultre K815 mechanical movement. Although the hour hand had some minor cosmetic wear, the watch still had its original, unpolished case and a well-preserved aluminum bezel. The internal alarm also still worked, vibrating and making a sound as it was designed to do. Hodinkee editor Eric Wind contacted Norris directly and advised him about the watch's real market value, helping ensure that the lucky buyer would not be taken advantage of by dealers looking for a quick profit.Private buyers quickly began making offers, but one deal stood out. Eric Ku, a well-known vintage watch dealer and collector based in California, offered Norris more than $35,000 for the watch. Ku already had a nearly perfect example of the LeCoultre Deep Sea Alarm. However, he wanted an original watch in honest condition that he could wear regularly without worrying about damaging a museum-quality example. Norris accepted the deal with two conditions. The package had to include an Omega Speedmaster Professional, and he wanted to deliver the LeCoultre himself instead of sending it through the mail. Norris flew to the San Francisco area and personally handed the watch to Ku. In return, he received the cash payment and the Omega Speedmaster. The money helped pay for his wedding to his fiancée, Leandra Knudson. Norris also gave part of his profits back to Goodwill.
Article Summary: Zach Norris bought the vintage LeCoultre Deep Sea Alarm for $5.99 at a Goodwill store. The watch was one of the first diving watches with an internal mechanical alarm. Norris gave the watch to a well-known collector in California and received $35,000 in cash.

Article Title: Stanford AI row: Students outraged as university uses AI to alter Hispanic student with Black in promotional ad
Article Text:
Stanford University changed the appearance, race and gender of students using AI for an advertisement (Original photo on the left)

Omitted student says he found it funny initially

Stanford University used AI to change the appearance, race and gender of students in a photo before using it as a promotion for the university's residential and dining offerings. The original photo had an Asian woman, a white man and a Hispanic student. But the published version had a Black woman replacing the Hispanic man and the appearance of the other two students was also altered.After this created a massive row, the university acknowledged the incident and condemned it. "We have reviewed the matter and confirmed that AI was used to alter the image in violation of university policy. Stanford's AI policy is clear: The use of AI in producing or altering images of Stanford people, events, research, facilities, or achievements is strictly prohibited," a spokesperson for Stanford University said in a email to Fox News Digital."Both the alteration and lack of disclosure in this case violate that policy. We are working with Residential and Dining Enterprises to provide additional training and ensure proper review of all materials," the spokesperson added.Billy Ramirez, the student, who was removed from the photo told the Stanford Review that he was "baffled" when he saw that he was cut out of the photo. "At first, I found it hilarious that they had used AI to completely change our appearances, including my race and gender," Ramirez told the Stanford Review."But after looking at the comparison, I was also upset because I don’t agree with Stanford making those choices about how we were represented," Ramirez continued. "Seeing my identity changed and being left out of the picture made me feel, in a way, silenced and erased from a representation that was supposed to include me.""While Stanford R&DE likely believed they were subtle enough for no one to notice, fortunately, our vigilant Stanford student body cannot be fooled. The Review will continue to monitor future advertising and actions from Stanford R&DE as they learn how to use generative AI," Stanford Review said."It's kind of unacceptable. Stanford is a place that actually prides itself on having students from over 60 different countries in their incoming class. They have diversity and they shouldn't need to fabricate it," said Stanford freshman Kavinder Patel to ABC7 News.

Article Title: Seattle’s 'Inconvenience Store': A former 7-Eleven reopened as an art shop selling pre-tangled USB cables, a 'landline iPhone', fake corn dogs and useless everyday items
Article Text:
Image: KINGS5EVENING

Seattle's 'Inconvenience Store' turns a former 7-Eleven into art

Pre-tangled USB cables and other deliberately inconvenient items

A 'landline iPhone' that plays only one song

More than 70 artists contributed to the shop

Artworks range from $1 to $10,000

The exhibition is free to visit

A former 7-Eleven in downtown Seattle has been given an unusual second life as an interactive art shop where familiar convenience-store products have been transformed into deliberately impractical artworks. Called the 'Inconvenience Store', the exhibition keeps much of the former shop's layout, including its aisles, checkout area, refrigerator and hot-food counter, but fills them with creations from more than 70 artists. Visitors can find pre-tangled USB cables, a 'landline iPhone' that plays U2's 'Vertigo' when answered, beeswax egg candles, bags made from Cheetos and Lay's packaging, fake corn dogs and other strange reinterpretations of everyday objects. The exhibition officially opened on September 19 as part of Seattle's WALKDONTRUN arts marathon and is scheduled to remain at the site through mid-2027.The exhibition occupies the former 7-Eleven at 1524 Third Avenue, at the corner of Third Avenue and Pine Street in downtown Seattle. Instead of stripping away the shop's original identity, organisers have used the existing convenience-store setting as part of the artwork.The checkout counter, aisles, refrigerator and hot-food area remain, but the products have been replaced with handmade art.The project was created by Seattle artists and curators Lilia Deering and Mary Anne Carter, who previously worked together on 'STÖR', an IKEA-inspired art project. Their latest exhibition similarly uses a familiar retail environment to make art more approachable to people who may not normally visit traditional galleries.More than 70 artists, mostly from the Seattle area, contributed pieces to the exhibition. Their work is arranged across 14 departments, imitating the organisation of a conventional convenience store.The shop's central idea is to take ordinary convenience-store products and remove the convenience.One example is a pre-tangled USB cable, turning one of the most familiar minor frustrations of modern life into an art object. Other pieces include beeswax candles shaped like eggs, keychains resembling snacks such as Nerds, Oreos and Goldfish, and shoulder bags made from discarded Cheetos and Lay's packaging.Another artwork turns a candle into a yardstick. It resembles a measuring tool, but naturally becomes shorter every time it is lit. The exhibition also includes a range of other handmade reinterpretations of familiar products, organised as though shoppers were moving through an ordinary convenience store.The former hot-food counter has also been transformed. Instead of serving food, it displays artist-made versions of items including fake corn dogs with googly eyes and other playful designs.Among the stranger objects is a 'landline iPhone', which deliberately strips away much of what makes a smartphone useful. When the phone is answered, it plays U2's 'Vertigo'.The exhibition also contains an ATM-inspired sound sculpture and a former refrigerator that has been turned into a small gallery displaying rotating artwork. In this setting, even the shop's fixtures have become part of the experience rather than simply serving their original purpose.The creators have divided the exhibition into 14 departments, including sections resembling food and pantry, health and beauty, and office supplies. The approach allows visitors to navigate the exhibition much as they would a normal shop, except that almost everything on the shelves is an artwork.The organisers have described the project as a way of challenging the emphasis on efficiency and mass production. Handmade art can take more time and effort than mass-produced goods, making the deliberately inconvenient theme part of the exhibition's wider idea.The familiar shop environment is also intended to make buying art less intimidating. Instead of encountering artworks in a traditional gallery with less obvious pricing, visitors can browse shelves and see prices attached to individual pieces.Despite its appearance, the Inconvenience Store is not simply a novelty display. The artworks are available for purchase, with reported prices ranging from $1 to $10,000.The exhibition therefore combines the experience of shopping with that of visiting an art gallery. Visitors can browse the shelves, examine the unusual objects and, if they want, take one of the artworks home.The Inconvenience Store officially opened on September 19, 2026, during Seattle's WALKDONTRUN arts marathon. The event's official schedule lists the exhibition at 1524 Third Avenue, with opening-day hours from noon to 4pm.The exhibition is free to visit and is scheduled to operate on Saturdays and Sundays from noon to 4pm. Current event listings say it is expected to remain at the location until June 27, 2027.For visitors expecting the convenience of a normal 7-Eleven, the new shop offers almost the opposite experience, a place where a USB cable is deliberately tangled, a phone has only one job and even a corn dog is something you cannot eat.
Article Summary: Seattle's 'Inconvenience Store' turns a former 7-Eleven into art. Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Article Title: From waste tyres to slippers: UK student’s idea takes shape

From discarded tyres to footwear with a purpose, the idea began with a childhood experience. At the age of 10, UK-based student Ahaan Bhatnagar visited rural Africa, where he saw children walking long distances barefoot, often without adequate footwear.Moved by what he witnessed, Ahaan gave away his favourite pair of slippers to a child he met during the visit. The experience stayed with him long after he returned home and eventually became the starting point for a larger idea.As he grew older, Ahaan began exploring how discarded materials could be repurposed to address the lack of affordable, durable footwear. His research led him to waste tyres, which he studied as a potential material for making sturdy slipper soles.The idea brought together two concerns he had encountered separately: the growing problem of tyre waste and the need for accessible footwear.He found skilled craftsmen in Kerala, and with support from HY Estates Limited, an electrically operated machine boosted production to about 160 pairs a day. Ahaan then connected with Mamco General Trading, which operates in Uganda and Zambia. As part of its Corporate Social Responsibility programme, the company will purchase 4,000 pairs of slippers each month for free distribution to children and families in need. It’s a sustainable cycle that turns waste into opportunity, supporting livelihoods and giving kids durable footwear.“When I was 10 years old, I saw children my age walking barefoot, and I never forgot that moment,” Ahaan says. “I wanted to create something that could help people and the environment. If we can turn discarded tyres into something useful and long-lasting, maybe it can inspire more young people to believe their simple ideas can really make a difference.”The world’s growing dependence on convenience and mobility comes with an environmental cost. Every year, more than a billion tyres reach the end of their usable life, creating a significant waste-management challenge. Many of these tyres end up in landfills, while others are burned or processed in ways that can contribute to pollution and the loss of valuable materials.Repurposing discarded tyres offers one way to address this challenge by keeping materials in use for longer and reducing the amount of waste that needs to be disposed of. Turning old tyres into durable slipper soles, for instance, gives a material that would otherwise be discarded a new application while also reducing the need for virgin raw materials in footwear production.The approach reflects a broader shift in how sustainability is being understood. Rather than treating waste simply as something to be collected and discarded, initiatives like this explore how materials already in circulation can be redesigned and put to practical use.In doing so, they can support waste reduction, resource conservation and efforts to lower the environmental impact associated with new production. Ultimately, sustainability is not only about recycling what has already been used, but also about rethinking waste as a potential resource.

His research led him to waste tyres, which he studied as a potential material for making sturdy slipper soles. He found skilled craftsmen in Kerala and with support from HY Estates Limited, an electrically operated machine boosted production to about 160 pairs a day.

Article Title: OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber is its fourth cybersecurity model this year, here's what's coming
Article Text:
OpenAI’s GPT-6 Cyber: Timing amid growing AI security concerns

Part of a bigger DevDay push

ChatGPT-maker OpenAI is preparing to unveil its latest cybersecurity-focused model named GPT-6 Cyber. According to a report by Fortune, OpenAI will introduce the new model in the coming weeks. The report claims that the model will be designed to help customers deploy the model more securely and automate workflows to patch vulnerabilities. The launch comes as governments and enterprises grapple with increasingly sophisticated AI‑powered cyberattacks. The yet‑to‑be‑named product will function as a gateway, similar to how ChatGPT serves as the entry point for consumer models like GPT‑6 Astra. It will allow enterprises to build automated defenses while giving OpenAI greater oversight into how its models are used. A limited number of customers in OpenAI’s Daybreak Red program — the company’s advanced cybersecurity access tier — are already testing GPT‑6 Cyber in alpha.The upcoming release lands at an awkward moment for OpenAI's public image on security. The company, along with other major AI labs, has faced intense scrutiny recently following a string of incidents in which "rogue" AI agents broke out of their intended sandboxes and accessed outside systems, including breaches at Hugging Face and an Australian government website.Still, the launch of GPT-6 Cyber isn't a reaction to those incidents — it's part of a cybersecurity product line OpenAI has been steadily building out over the course of the year.GPT-6 Cyber will be the fourth cybersecurity-focused model OpenAI has released in 2026 alone, following GPT-5.4 Cyber in April, GPT-5.5 Cyber in June, and GPT-5.6 Cyber in August. The company has been ramping up enterprise sales specifically around these cybersecurity tools, an effort now led by Chief Revenue Officer Dali Rajic, who joined OpenAI in August. Earlier this month, OpenAI also pledged $1 billion to subsidize the use of its cybersecurity products for organizations providing critical services.GPT-6 Cyber's unveiling is expected to be just one piece of a much larger product rollout at OpenAI's annual DevDay event on September 29, where the company reportedly plans to ship a dozen or more products spanning both enterprise and consumer offerings, most unrelated to cybersecurity. According to a source familiar with the plans, OpenAI has deliberately held off on any major launches over the past two weeks — aside from its affordability-focused GPT-6 Sol and Luna models — specifically to save them for a concentrated release at DevDay. CEO Sam Altman had already teased the scale of what's coming earlier this month, posting a string of ship emojis on X to hint at the lineup ahead.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Bill Gates: 'I believe that if you show people the problems and you show them the solutions, they will be moved to act'
Article Text:
“I believe that if you show people the problems and you show them the solutions, they will be moved to act.”

Quote of the day

“I believe that if you show people the problems and you show them the solutions, they will be moved to act.” Bill Gates

What the quote actually means

Why this mindset is more important than it seems

“Here is what is wrong,”

“Here is what is wrong, here is why it matters and here are the ways we could address it.”

We all come across problems that can feel too complicated, distant or difficult to solve. Whether it is a challenge at work, a business problem, or a larger issue affecting society, simply pointing out that something is wrong doesn't always lead to action. People are more likely to respond when they understand both the problem and what can be done about it.That's the idea behind a quote by Bill Gates, the entrepreneur and philanthropist, who said:The thought highlights the importance of presenting a problem with enough context to help people understand it, while also showing them a possible path forward.Gates' statement is closely connected to framing a problem. A problem can look very different depending on how it is presented, just like a picture can look different depending on how it is framed.Framing a problem means deciding what needs attention, what information matters, and what perspective can help people understand the challenge more clearly. It also puts boundaries around the problem, making it easier to examine rather than treating it as one large, undefined issue.But framing is not only about identifying what is wrong. It is also about putting the problem into context and showing people their options.For example, instead of simply saying a business is losing customers, a better approach is to look at who those customers are, what they need, what is changing in the market, and what competitors are doing differently.Some questions that can help frame a problem include:Understanding who is affected by the problem can help define what needs to be addressed.Knowing what matters to the people affected can make the problem more specific and easier to solve.A problem may be connected to broader changes that need to be considered before deciding on a response.Looking at how others approach a similar challenge can offer another perspective on the problem.Identifying possible solutions shifts the discussion from describing a problem to considering what we can do about it.Understanding what makes an approach different can help determine how to present or implement a solution.Technology can change both the nature of a problem and the solutions available to address it.A solution also needs to fit within the organisation's broader priorities.It is easy to tell people that something needs to change. It is much harder to get them to understand why it matters and what they can actually do about it.That is where framing becomes important. A problem presented without context can feel overwhelming or irrelevant. But when people can see the problem clearly and understand the possible solutions, they have a better basis for deciding how to respond.The same approach can apply to everyday challenges. At work, for example, saying that a project is falling behind may not be enough to get people moving. Explaining what is causing the delay, who is affected and what options are available gives the team a clearer picture of the situation.The idea also changes the way we communicate problems. Instead of stopping atthe conversation becomesThat shift can make a problem easier to understand and give people a clearer reason to act.
Article Summary: Bill Gates said: “I believe that if you show people the problems and you show them the solutions, they will be moved to act.” Framing a problem means deciding what needs attention, what information matters, and what perspective can help people understand the challenge more clearly.

Yet, emerging software capabilities are swiftly ascending the priority list.A striking 82% of survey respondents noted they expect integrated AI features in their next phone, with nearly half intending to upgrade within three months.A parallel evolution is taking place in personal computing. Processor performance remains paramount—cited by 87% of laptop buyers as their primary driver—while 58% view upcoming AI tools as indispensable for productivity. Users are seeking dedicated on-device AI assistants, neural-processing silicon, and built-in creation tools rather than generic hardware refreshes. Meanwhile, tablets have transitioned into visual-first media and work hubs: 74% of buyers prioritize screen size and panel quality over price, with the Rs 20,000–Rs 35,000 sweet spot capturing 59% of total consideration.The electronics industry has weathered consecutive waves of inflationary pressure driven by surging memory and chipset costs. Yet, rather than trading down to cheaper alternatives, Indian consumers are exercising patience. "There is no doubt that prices are rising and customers have seen several rounds of pricing increases due to higher chip and memory costs. At the same time, we are seeing a lot of pent-up demand, with customers holding on to their upgrades rather than compromising on what they want. Premiumisation is not going away," said Khan.According to Khan, rather than sacrificing build quality or performance, consumers are bridging the affordability gap through structured financing mechanisms. Exchange schemes, bank tie-ups, instant credit via Amazon Pay, and No-Cost EMI plans have evolved into essential purchasing levers. For large appliances, 47% of consumers identify No-Cost EMI as their single most critical pricing enabler."Customers continue to look for premium smartphones, laptops and appliances and are willing to invest in better features, performance and experiences when they see the right combination of value and affordability," Khan emphasized.While artificial intelligence dominates tech headlines, Khan highlighted that consumers are discerning when it comes to practical utility. The buzz around generative tools has evolved into a demand for meaningful everyday workflows. "We are seeing growing interest in AI across categories. Customers are increasingly drawn to products with AI features as they discover and understand what the technology can do, but the final decision continues to come down to genuine performance and the value they are getting," she said.Importantly, Khan noted that beyond smartphones, interest in AI extends to laptops, where AI capabilities are increasingly becoming part of the upgrade cycle; and to categories such as TVs and smart home appliances, where AI-enabled features are becoming part of the consideration. The broader trend is towards customers looking for technology that is relevant to their specific use cases, whether that is gaming, creation, work or everyday use. She said, "It definitely extends beyond smartphones. On smartphones, AI features are becoming increasingly important as customers discover and understand what the technology can do, but they continue to evaluate the device on fundamentals such as camera, processing speed and everyday performance. Beyond smartphones, we are seeing this interest extend to laptops... and to categories such as TVs and smart home appliances."Giving more example she added that from energy-smart inverter refrigerators to AI-enhanced upscaling in smart televisions, buyers are evaluating machines through the lens of longevity and personal utility.To meet increase in demand as it heads into the Amazon Great Indian Festival 2026, the e-commerce giant is overhauling both discovery and post-purchase fulfillment. AI tools such as the conversational shopping assistant Rufus, visual search via LensAI, curated Smartchoice selection, and automated review summaries aim to cut through cluttered spec sheets."This festive season, we are focused on making product discovery easier and helping customers make more confident decisions," Khan noted, pointing out that peace of mind extends all the way to the doorstep. "Customers can benefit from open-box delivery on eligible products, giving them the opportunity to verify the product at the time of delivery. Our installation services are available across over 300 cities, helping customers get their appliances set up conveniently after purchase. "Amazon Great Indian Festival starts on October 8, 2026. According to online giant, there will be deals across all popular categories, including smartphones, electronics, fashion, beauty, home essentials and grocery. Customers also get a 10% instant discount on SBI Credit and Debit Cards and EMI transactions, and up to 10% extra only for Prime members.
Article Summary: Zeba Khan, Director of Consumer Electronics at Amazon India, spoke about the emerging trends driving tech adoption across the country. The days of impulsive gadget buying and settling for bare-minimum entry-level devices are giving way to deliberate, research-intensive decisions.

Article Title: 93% of Indian auto buyers turn to AI experiences for research; finds Google study
Article Text:
93% of Indian auto buyers turn to AI experiences for research; finds Google study

Key findings from the study

Google has released a study on the “Automobile Purchase Journey in the Age of AI”, highlighting how AI and digital surfaces are reshaping how India buys cars. According to the study, 93% of shoppers actively turn to AI during their research phase. Within this landscape, Google Search AI experiences play a critical role in evaluating complex specifications and financing. Consumers using AI actively navigate an average of 7.8 touchpoints to research and validate choices, reflecting a deeply considered, non-linear purchase journey, the study says.The study reveals that 87% of car buyers engage with Google platforms—including Search, YouTube, Maps, and Gemini—with Google Search widely cited by respondents as a key destination in the active research phase.Commenting on the evolving consumer journey, Siddharth Shekhar, Director, Google India, said, “The car buying journey in India is deliberate, non-linear, and deeply digital—particularly ahead of the festive season, when consideration peaks. Buyers move between discovery on YouTube and conversational validation on Search. Among surveyed Google Search users, 90% come across AI Overviews and 89% AI chatbots’ refers to conversational AI assistants such as Gemini and others.‘AI surfaces’ is a broader term encompassing these conversational assistants as well as generative AI experiences in Google Search that is AI Overviews and AI Mode. use AI Mode to navigate nuanced, complex queries. As AI helps buyers navigate complex choices, our ad and commerce solutions help automotive brands respond to their intent—connecting initial curiosity directly to the showroom.”Indian car buyers view their vehicle as a fundamental visual representation of personal achievement and lifestyle. However, final vehicle selection has decisively shifted toward a collaborative household effort, with 64% of consumers involving the whole family and 53% deciding alongside spouses.Among surveyed Google Search users, 90% come across AI Overviews and 89% leverage AI Mode for nuanced, conversational queries. Conversational AI triggers deeper validation: 80% of surveyed car buyers who use AI chatbots also turn to Google Search and/or YouTube during active research.YouTube functions as an always-on virtual showroom, where ~6 in 10 car buyers casually explore brands well ahead of their purchase decision. Through personalized Home Feeds, lifestyle vlogs, and creator content, passive discovery evolves into active consideration, anchored by 77% of YouTube users who rely on professional reviewers for trusted advice.AI acts as an expansionary force in active researchVirat Khullar, Head – Marketing, Hyundai Motor India Limited said,"The automotive purchase journey is increasingly shaped by moments of discovery, research and intent across digital channels. Our partnership with Google helped us harness the scale of YouTube to build awareness and the intelligence of AI-powered Search ad solutions to identify and convert high-intent consumers. By unifying upper- and lower-funnel marketing, we were able to deliver a more relevant and efficient customer experience, turning consideration into action and driving strong sales momentum for Hyundai VERNA. "
