Article Title: Meta unveils camera-free Ray-Ban Audio glasses and a keychain AI companion at Connect 2026
Article Text:
Ray-Ban Meta Audio : cameras out, all-day wearability in

Muse Charm: an AI agent you can put on a keychain

At its annual Meta Connect event, Facebook-parent Meta has announced a major expansion of its consumer hardware portfolio with the launch of new Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses and a quirky Muse AI keychain. The new products unveiled highlight Meta’s AI push to embed AI agents into everyday life simply by blending fashion, utility and entertainment. The new Ray-Ban Meta glasses lineup builds on Meta’s partnership with EssilorLuxottica. The glasses now feature deeper AI integration, including voice-controlled access to Meta’s AI assistant, improved audio quality, and enhanced camera capabilities. On the other hand, Meta Muse AI keychain is a pocket-sized device described as “Tamagotchi-like.” The gadget acts as a portable AI agent, offering playful interactions, reminders, and personalized assistance. Meta positioned Muse as a way to make AI more approachable, turning everyday tasks into engaging experiences.The headline hardware announcement was Ray-Ban Meta Audio, Meta's first-ever camera-free smart glasses, developed through its ongoing partnership with EssilorLuxottica. By ditching the camera setup entirely, Meta managed to bring the glasses down to just 43 grams — noticeably lighter than the roughly 50g standard Ray-Ban Meta models and far lighter than the 70g Display glasses — while still packing in hands-free music and podcast playback, calling, and conversations with Meta's AI assistant.The glasses come in Clubmaster and Burbank styles, with customizable temple tips, nose pads, and overextension hinges for a more tailored fit, and support a wide range of optical prescriptions.Battery life is rated at up to 12 hours on a single charge, extendable to roughly 48 additional hours using the included charging case. Ray-Ban Meta Audio launches October 13 at $349, with pre-orders open now.Meta also used the moment to introduce Hearing Enhancement, an FDA-cleared accessibility feature arriving later this year for supported AI glasses. Using the glasses' six-speaker array, the feature is designed to help people who are hard of hearing pick out speech more clearly in noisy environments, letting users adjust left-right audio balance or shift to mono audio in one ear. Meta is pricing it at $149.99 as a one-time purchase, or bundling it into a Meta One subscription, framing it as a notably more affordable alternative to traditional hearing aids, which the company says typically start around $800. A 30-day free trial will also be available.Beyond the audio-only model, Meta also refreshed its standard Ray-Ban Meta line with the Gen 3 glasses, adding a slimmer build, longer battery life, a 12MP camera, and 3K Ultra HD video recording. The company additionally previewed a new hologram calling feature for Ray-Ban Meta Display users, letting someone do a quick self-capture with their phone to generate a hologram visible to whoever they're calling — expected to arrive in early access on WhatsApp in the US within the next few months.The event's true "one more thing" moment came when CEO Mark Zuckerberg unveiled Muse Charm, a small, palm-sized wearable designed to give people another physical way to interact with Muse, Meta's recently launched and increasingly popular personal AI agent.The device houses a tiny screen displaying Jolly, the cute animated avatar Meta has built to represent Muse, and is meant to be carried in a pocket or clipped onto a keychain. Zuckerberg explained that the team condensed the entire Muse experience — including its real-time voice and avatar system — into a device small enough to live on a keychain while remaining constantly available to talk to. A fingerprint sensor built into the corner of the device lets users start a conversation instantly, without needing to unlock a phone or open an app first. For anyone not wearing AI glasses, Zuckerberg positioned Muse Charm as the fastest possible way to talk to Muse and show it what's happening around you.The gadget leans into a distinctly Tamagotchi-like aesthetic — small, personality-driven, and designed to keep users continually engaged with Meta's AI software. Zuckerberg acknowledged the hardware isn't quite ready for release, saying the team still needs to finalize how its internal components are laid out, but confirmed Muse Charm is on track to ship in time for the December holiday season.
Article Summary: Muse AI keychain is a pocket-sized device described as “Tamagotchi-like” The gadget acts as a portable AI agent, offering playful interactions, reminders, and personalized assistance. Ray-Ban Meta Audio is Meta's first-ever camera-free smart glasses, developed through its partnership with EssilorLuxottica.

Article Title: Apple Siri settlement: iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 16 owners can now claim up to $95; here's how to file
Article Text:
Only US buyers of seven iPhone models qualify for the payout

Filing an Apple Siri settlement claim needs your iPhone serial number

Claims close on December 21, but payments will wait until 2027

Apple has opened the claims window for its $250 million (about Rs 2,200 crore) settlement over the delayed Apple Intelligence upgrade to Siri. Eligible iPhone owners in the US can now file for a payout of $25 per device. That figure could rise to $95, depending on how many people come forward.The class action, Landsheft et al. v. Apple Inc., accused the company of selling the iPhone 16 as "built for Apple Intelligence" while the smarter Siri shown at WWDC 2024 was nowhere near ready. That upgraded Siri only reached users with iOS 27 earlier this month, more than two years after its first demo. Apple has denied any wrongdoing, and the settlement terms say it is not an admission of liability.The claim covers purchases made between June 10, 2024, and March 29, 2025. The iPhone 15 Pro and 15 Pro Max qualify, along with the entire iPhone 16 lineup: the iPhone 16, 16 Plus, 16 Pro, 16 Pro Max and the budget iPhone 16e.You must be the original buyer, and the phone must have been bought for personal or work use, not resale. Indian buyers of the same models are not covered, since the case was filed and settled in the US.Claims are filed on the official website, SmartphoneAISettlement.com.The form asks for your name, address, phone number and the iPhone's serial number, which you'll find under Settings > General > About. If you don't have the serial number, the form will take your Apple Account email and the phone number linked to the device instead.Eligible owners should also receive an email over the coming days with a claim ID and PIN. You can still file without them. Each device needs its own claim, and only one payment is allowed per phone.The $95 maximum depends on how many iPhone owners filePayouts start at $25 per device and can climb to $95 if fewer valid claims come in than expected. Payment options include PayPal, Venmo, direct deposit and a paper check.Ryan Clarkson, co-lead counsel on the case and founder of Clarkson Law Firm, described the fund as the largest false advertising settlement on record.The deadline to file is December 21, 2026. A federal district court in San Jose will hold the final approval hearing on February 24, 2027, and payments will only go out after that. Any appeal could delay them further.Anyone unsure about eligibility can call the settlement administrator on 1-888-988-8945. For those who bought an iPhone 16 waiting for the new Siri, the money will arrive even later than the feature did.
Article Summary: Claims close on December 21, but payments will wait until 2027. Only US buyers of seven iPhone models qualify for the payout. Each device needs its own claim, and only one payment is allowed per phone. Payment options include PayPal, Venmo, direct deposit and a paper check.

Article Title: BenQ showcases MOBIUZ gaming monitor line-up at Tokyo Game Show 2026
Article Text:
BenQ showcases MOBIUZ gaming monitor line-up at Tokyo Game Show 2026

BenQ showcased its MOBIUZ gaming monitor line-up at Tokyo Game Show 2026 held at Makuhari Messe from September 17 to 20, under the theme, "MOBIUZ Game Art Museum.” The theme centres on how MOBIUZ monitors reproduce the work of game creators through this colour tuning, treating each title's visual identity as something to be faithfully rendered rather than simply displayed.At the heart of this year's showcase is Game Art Color HDR, a new firmware feature that builds on BenQ's existing Smart Game Art technology. The feature introduces three HDR presets (Immersive, Balanced and Vivid) for each game art colour mode, giving players finer control over how a title's colour palette and contrast are reproduced on screen. It is available across BenQ's three premium OLED models (EX271UZ, EX321UZ, EX271QZ) and three of its latest QHD models (EX271QMZ, EX271QM, EX271QP), six displays in all.Rajeev Singh, Managing Director, BenQ India and South Asia, said, “Gaming today is as much about a title's visual identity as it is about performance, and Indian gamers are increasingly discerning about both. Game Art Color HDR, MOBIUZ users can experience a game the way its creators intended, whether that's the painterly warmth of a fantasy title or the stark contrast of a sci-fi world. As India's gaming and esports audience continues to grow, this is the kind of display innovation we’re bringing closer to our market.Speaking on the BenQ MOBIUZ range, Jeffrey Liang, President, BenQ Asia Pacific, said, "The Game Art Museum concept is really about how closely we work with game creators on colour science. Game Art Color HDR is a direct result of that: it lets a monitor read a title's art direction and respond to it. As APAC becomes one of the fastest-growing regions for PC and console gaming, that kind of art-led engineering is what will differentiate MOBIUZ as the category matures. ”Beyond the display wall, the Tokyo booth gave visitors a dedicated area to compare each model's performance side by side, and a hands-on zone to try anticipated game titles in MOBIUZ's flagship setup. This ran alongside exhibits featuring game developers speaking to their own creative choices around visuals and world-building, the same choices Game Art Color HDR is built to reproduce on screen.
Article Summary: BenQ showcased its MOBIUZ gaming monitor line-up at Tokyo Game Show 2026 held at Makuhari Messe from September 17 to 20. At the heart of this year's showcase is Game Art Color HDR, a new feature that builds on BenQ's existing Smart Game Art technology.

Article Title: Microsoft says it has taken down ‘AI chatbot built for cybercrime’ that hacked 12,000-plus emails across over 10,000 organisations globally
Article Text:
Targets in several countries, including India

How the scam actually worked

Microsoft has said that it has thwarted an effort to shut down a subscription-based scam platform that relied on an AI chatbot to break into more than 12,000 Microsoft accounts over the course of a few months. The platform, called EvilTokens, first surfaced on a Telegram channel back in February, charging users an initial fee of $1,500 followed by a recurring monthly charge of $500. EvilTokens essentially offered a one-stop service that streamlined nearly every step needed to compromise email accounts at scale. According to the company, once inside, the platform helped its customers sift through victims' inboxes, identify the most targets and even draft follow-up emails designed to trick employees into transferring funds into accounts controlled by the attackers.“In short, AI was not simply helping attackers write more convincing messages. It helped them decide who to target, who to impersonate, and how to most effectively exploit the relationship to extract as much money as possible,” the company said.Microsoft says that while it also attacked specific countries, its significance extends beyond its rapid growth and global reach.“Microsoft observed the highest concentrations of victim activity in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia, India, and France.Affected organizations ranged from wholesale distribution and construction to financial services, real estate, higher education, and healthcare. Working with partners, Microsoft seized 50 websites used to operate the service and disabled more than 150 additional domains tied to its supporting infrastructure. In the United Kingdom, the Metropolitan Police Service’s cybercrime team arrested two men on suspicion of offenses connected with the alleged operation of EvilTokens,” the company said.According to Microsoft, what set EvilTokens apart was the AI-style chatbot sitting at the heart of the operation. The chatbot could analyse a victim's inbox and help criminals pinpoint trusted relationships, payment approval authority, sensitive job responsibilities and other circumstances where fraud was most likely to succeed. It could even go a step further, recommending specific fraud strategies and drafting messages impersonating trusted contacts to manipulate victims into taking action.The account compromises were carried out through a legitimate OAuth authentication process known as device code authentication. This method was originally designed for devices like smart TVs, essentially anything lacking a standard login interface. In this setup, the device being signed into displays a code, and the user is instructed to enter that code into a browser on a separate device, which then gets authenticated.EvilTokens gave its customers a platform capable of automating the mass sending of spam emails. Anyone who clicked on a malicious link or attachment inside these emails would be redirected to a webpage running a hidden automation script, which interacted in real time with the victim's Microsoft identity provider to generate a device code that would enrol a device belonging to the attacker.The victim would then see this device code onscreen, along with instructions telling them to copy it and enter it into Microsoft's official device login portal. Behind the scenes, complex backend operations allowed the hackers slip past traditional signature- or pattern-based security detection systems. This technique powered the entire attack chain, from generating dynamic device codes all the way through to actions taken after an account was compromised.Microsoft said EvilTokens marks a significant shift in how mass account compromises, and everything that follows them, now unfold.
Article Summary: Microsoft says it has thwarted an effort to shut down a subscription-based scam platform that relied on an AI chatbot. The platform, called EvilTokens, first surfaced on a Telegram channel back in February, charging users an initial fee of $1,500 followed by a recurring monthly charge of $500. According to the company, once inside, the platform helped its customers sift through victims' inboxes, identify the most targets and even draft follow-up emails.

Article Title: Adobe Premiere mobile app now available on Android: What it means for users
Article Text:
“Today, we’re excited to share that Adobe Premiere on mobile is now available on Android for free”,

“With 95% of Indian creators already being mobile-first, the smartphone is fast becoming the studio for India’s next generation of creators. We're excited to offer Premiere mobile on iOS and now on Android devices, putting Adobe’s pro-quality video tools into the hands of millions of creators in India for free.”

Adobe Premiere mobile Android availability

Adobe Premiere mobile app : Key features

More features coming to Adobe Premiere mobile app

Adobe has expanded its Premiere mobile video editing app to Android, bringing it to a wider range of users after launching it on iPhone last year. The Android version is free and includes tools for editing video, audio, effects, and other content on mobile devices. The app supports video editing and export at up to 4K resolution, along with a multi-track timeline and AI-powered features from Adobe Firefly. Adobe says Premiere mobile is available on devices running Android 13 or later with at least 5GB of RAM.said Diksha Kuhar, Director, Product Marketing, Premiere mobile, Adobe.Adobe Premiere mobile is now available through the Google Play Store for Android devices running Android 13 or later.The company specifies a minimum requirement of 5GB of RAM.The Android version includes Enhance Audio, which reduces background noise and improves the clarity of interviews, voiceovers, and other recordings. It also offers frame-accurate editing and a multi-track timeline that lets users layer video, music, text, and effects.Users can also start projects with creator-made templates or create their own. The app includes effects, transitions, creative assets, and music from Adobe Stock, plus the ability to use files stored on the device or extract audio from videos.Adobe Premiere mobile supports editing and exporting videos at up to 4K. Adobe says the app does not require a forced login or show upgrade prompts during editing.The app also includes generative AI features powered by Adobe Firefly. These include Generative Fill, Image-to-Video and Generate Sound Effects. Adobe says the mobile experience is also ad-free and does not add a watermark to edited videos.Adobe says it plans to add more features to the mobile app, including Adobe Fonts, enhanced captions, keyframes, cropping, beat detection and continued editing between Premiere mobile and Premiere on desktop. The free version includes the core video editing tools, while additional generative credits and storage are available through upgrades.Adobe has also shared feedback from creators using Premiere mobile. Adhiraj Singh Anand said Enhance Audio helps him clean up sound after recording in uncontrolled environments, while Mohanraj Thangaraj said he uses the app to edit drone, camera and phone footage into short-form videos while travelling.Katarina Mogus highlighted the app's YouTube Shorts templates for creating and publishing videos while on the go. Vimal Sharma said the Android version gives him access to video editing tools, including sound enhancement and frame-level control, without needing a laptop.
Article Summary: Adobe has expanded its Premiere mobile video editing app to Android. The Android version is free and includes tools for editing video, audio, effects, and other content. The app supports video editing and export at up to 4K resolution, along with a multi-track timeline.
